newsitem.title: USA: 3Com shares rise on Siemens pact, bullish outlook.
newsitem.headline: 3Com shares rise on Siemens pact, bullish outlook.

text.p: 3Com Corp. shares jumped Wednesday after the computer networking equipment maker said it will work with German telecommunications company Siemens AG to develop products that can handle both computer data and voice telephone calls.
A respected Wall Street analyst also said 3Com's stock could rise to $65 in the next 12 to 18 months based on the company's earnings and revenue prospects.
Stock in 3Com, the second-biggest networking company, rose $2.563 to $52.625 on Nasdaq, where it was the most active issue on volume of 21.2 million shares.

3Com said it will work with Siemens to develop entirely new networking products that would enable companies to combine their telephone and computer networks into one network. This would let customers place phone calls via the Internet, or conduct video conferences through personal computers.
Under the agreement, Siemens also will sell 3Com networking gear worldwide.
"There's no reason to change 3Com's revenue or earnings forecasts, but it's a good move for 3Com," said Martin Pyykkonen, analyst at investment bank Furman Selz.

3Com also got a boost from Joseph Bellace, a closely watched networking analyst at Merrill Lynch & Co. Bellace upgraded 3Com's stock to "accumulate" from "neutral" based on the company's improving prospects.

Stock in 3Com, based in Santa Clara, Calif., had plunged in recent months because of concerns that competitors, like Intel Corp. and Cisco Systems Inc., are cutting into its profits. Some investors also were concerned that 3Com paid too much recently to acquire modem maker U.S. Robotics Corp.
Bellace wrote in a report that he expects 3Com to report a modest increase in profits this quarter, counting U.S. Robotics' results. But per-share earnings could rise 31 percent in 1998, he said.
